description: Conditionally loaded reference node graph. The entry risk judgment selects the lane: Low takes the low-fast-path single-node exclusive lane, and an explicit Oracle request or Medium/High takes the oracle lane with the common entry. When a node when is satisfied, load its full path together with its requires edges, and do not load unrelated nodes. Each node's when is the canonical load condition. SKILL.md restates them as prose on purpose, because the agent reads SKILL.md at runtime and may never open this file — the copy is a projection, not a duplicate to delete, and skill-contract.test.mjs fails when a loader:agent node is missing from that section.

entryContract.firstToolCall: Read exactly one lane entry node — low-fast-path when risk=Low, otherwise common
entryContract.responseHeader: risk=<Low|Medium|High> lane=<low-fast-path|oracle> nodes=[node ids actually Read]
entryContract.appliesTo: both implementation requests and explanation·plan-only requests
entryContract.loadConditionRule: Read when as the decision point, not the deliverable stage — load it the moment you make the decision that node owns, and the same holds when you answer only with examples·structure·plans without writing files. If applicability is ambiguous, load. Whether to skip a load is not a judgment call.

lanes.escalation: immediately disqualified when a policy question·new contract·architecture decision appears — promote to the oracle lane

carveOut.when: only part of the request disqualifies — escalate that part alone and finish the remainder in this lane
requiresAll: the remainder touches no state, no side effect, and no type the carved-out scope reads or writes
the remainder is correct whichever way the carved-out policy is decided
the remainder is separately verifiable and separately revertible
carveOut.otherwise: promote the whole request — a split that shares a failure is worse than the ceremony it avoided
carveOut.record: one descope line naming what was carved out, its trigger, and where it went; the Oracle card registers the remainder under Non-goals

bundleContract.purpose: Deterministic pre-joined reads of the same reference bytes. A bundle exists to stabilize the prompt prefix so a repeat session hits the cache, and never to summarize or replace node content.
rules: A bundle is optional. Reading its nodes individually is always valid and produces the same bytes.
Report the node ids in the lane header, never the bundle id.
Never hand-edit bundles/ — edit the reference node and regenerate.
A bundle contains every requires edge of its declared nodes, in dependency-first order.

A continuation bundle (`after`) delivers only the nodes its base bundles did not; the header lists the assumed nodes. Read it only when the base bundle's nodes are already in context — reading base + continuation equals reading the full lane node set once.
